title: "Insert-size counts: riker 0.4.1, native and projected SQL"
output: github_document
params:

  repo: "."
  extension: "build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension"
  riker: !r Sys.getenv("RIKER_BIN")

## Contract and declared targets

Fulcrum Genomics **riker 0.4.1** (MIT), tag
`40d5e3260c5b1b9d210c28f7c90a75387013b4ce`, is the external oracle.
Picard is context only. Integer counts must match exactly; mean, population
standard deviation, median and MAD must match riker's serialized two decimal
places exactly. Both directions of each relation comparison are checked.

Targets are declared before any timed run:

- Every BAM/CRAM, arm, thread count and scale must satisfy exact parity.
- At 1×, each DuckHTS arm's median elapsed time divided by riker's must be
  **<= 1.05 at 1 thread, <= 1.00 at 2, and <= 0.90 at 4 and 8**, independently
  for BAM and CRAM. Apply these targets to native and projected SQL separately.
- Report the native/projected-SQL elapsed-time ratio without a pass/fail gate;
  this comparison informs the supervisor's final public-name decision.
- For each arm/format/thread count whose 1× median is at least 5 seconds,
  the 1×/2×/4× log-time/log-input exponent must be **<= 1.25**.
- Peak process RSS must be **<= 256 MiB overhead + 3× declared live state**.
  Live state includes worst-case overlapping per-worker sparse hash tables
  (16.25 bytes/slot, power-of-two capacity at <= .77 load), 8 MiB decoder
  state per handle, one merged hash table and 24 bytes per output count bin.
  This is a hypothesis to test, not an assertion about measured htslib usage.
- No spill is allowed. DuckDB has a 2 GiB buffer limit and zero temporary
  storage allowance; a worker error is a failed run, not a discarded trial.

Full workloads use registry artifacts `roh_mixture_hg00403_chr20_cram` and
`insert_size_hg00403_chr20_bam`; the latter is a network-free BAM transcode of
that CRAM using `liftover_grch38_fasta` and RBCFTools' bundled samtools. Stage
with `benchmarks/insert_size_stage.R` after checking disk space; the function
also checks the 8 GiB free-space floor with a 6 GiB staging reserve. No full
HG00188 BAM is staged. The smoke workload and SQL reference are checksum-pinned
committed fixtures staged through `insert-size-smoke` in the same registry.

Each arm runs in a fresh R process (a fresh DuckDB process for native/SQL),
with thread settings 1/2/4/8. Native settings are histogram workers, projected
SQL settings are DuckDB processing threads, and riker settings are its own
`--threads` semantics; these are not identical worker models. Native/SQL use
zero additional htslib decompression workers. The full matrix has three
replicates and 1×/2×/4× complete file scans, with output materialization on each
scan; scales do not change bin cardinality. This measures scaling in records,
not scaling in distinct insert sizes. `/usr/bin/time` measures end-to-end
worker wall time and maximum RSS, including R startup, input decoding,
reduction, metrics and output materialization. riker also writes its plot;
DuckHTS emits counts/metrics/histogram relations, not a plot. This output-cost
difference must accompany any speed comparison.

Independent riker raw and default outputs are prepared outside measured
workers. All worker results are compared against them; no failed comparison is
filtered. Record denominators come from registry identities, retained pair
and bin denominators from riker's untrimmed histogram. Summary moments trim
tails without changing original pair counts. Smoke runs invoke all 24
format/arm/thread combinations with **no clock or RSS measurement**.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
repo <- normalizePath(params$repo, mustWork = TRUE)
source(file.path(repo, "benchmarks/insert_size_driver.R"))
result <- run_insert_size_benchmark(repo, params$extension, params$riker, params$smoke)
```

## Results

```{r results, results='asis'}
rows <- result$rows
if (result$smoke) {
  cat("**Reduced smoke only; no timed comparison was run.**\n\n")
  cat(sum(rows$parity), "fresh-process checks passed; exact raw integer counts and rounded metrics/histograms agree.\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(rows[, c("format", "arm", "threads", "records", "read_pairs", "bins",
                             "metric_rows", "histogram_rows", "parity")]))
  cat("\nSpeed, RSS and scaling criteria: **not measured**. Spill: disabled for native/SQL.\n")
} else {
  print(knitr::kable(rows))
  cat("\nRSS criterion:", if (all(rows$peak_rss_mib <= rows$rss_budget_mib)) "PASS" else "FAIL", "\n\n")
  medians <- aggregate(seconds ~ format + arm + threads + scale, rows, median)
  gates <- list()
  for (format in unique(rows$format)) {
    for (threads in unique(rows$threads)) {
      selected <- medians[medians$format == format & medians$threads == threads, ]
      one <- selected[selected$scale == 1, ]
      times <- setNames(one$seconds, one$arm)
      target <- c(`1` = 1.05, `2` = 1.00, `4` = .90, `8` = .90)[[as.character(threads)]]
      gates[[length(gates) + 1L]] <- data.frame(format, threads, target,
        native_sql_ratio = times[["native"]] / times[["projected_sql"]],
        native_riker_ratio = times[["native"]] / times[["riker"]],
        sql_riker_ratio = times[["projected_sql"]] / times[["riker"]],
        native_pass = times[["native"]] / times[["riker"]] <= target,
        sql_pass = times[["projected_sql"]] / times[["riker"]] <= target)
      for (arm in unique(selected$arm)) {
        arm_rows <- selected[selected$arm == arm, ]
        if (times[[arm]] >= 5) {
          exponent <- unname(coef(lm(log(seconds) ~ log(scale), arm_rows))[[2L]])
          cat(format, threads, arm, "scaling exponent", exponent,
              if (exponent <= 1.25) "PASS" else "FAIL", "\n\n")
        } else cat(format, threads, arm, "scaling gate not applicable (1x < 5 s).\n\n")
      }
    }
  }
  print(knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, gates)))
}
```

## Interpretation and next measurement

The native reducer is expected to beat projected SQL because it avoids emitting
one DuckDB row and one CIGAR string per alignment, SQL flag/orientation
expressions, and the per-record hash aggregate. The same HTS decoding and CRAM
reference I/O remain. This is an expectation, not measured performance evidence.
The nearest recorded BAM-reduction baseline is
`benchmarks/benchmark_bam_mismatch_counts.md`; it exercises a different kernel
and cannot establish insert-size throughput or regression status.

Profile scan/decode time, CRAM reference fetches, task-window overlap decoding,
histogram hash operations and merge time separately. At multiple threads,
inspect storage throughput and per-handle decompression before changing task
sizes or adding SIMD. Compare an explicitly sequential native scan against
indexed scans to quantify index and repeated-overlap costs. Very short inputs
will be dominated by fresh-process startup and riker plotting. The full chr20
matrix, 1×/2×/4× measurements and RSS ceilings remain for the quiet-host run;
none can be inferred from this smoke.
